note: Bite-size notes from Apoorva's academic questions, written in plain words by Claude. One entry per topic; repeated questions update the same entry.

items.title: ASA physical status
points: Grades the patient's overall health before anaesthesia: I healthy, II mild disease, III severe disease with limitation, IV constant threat to life, V moribund, VI brain-dead donor; add E for emergency.
Current version amended Dec 2020: definitions unchanged, adult/paediatric/obstetric examples added.
Handy cut-offs: BMI 30–40 = II, ≥40 = III; MI/stroke/stent <3 months = IV, >3 months = III; normal pregnancy = II.
Describes the patient, not the surgery; inter-rater agreement only fair–moderate, II vs III most disputed.
items.pearl: Grade = clinical judgement; the examples are guides, not rules.

items.title: Pressure support ventilation (PSV)
points: Patient-triggered, pressure-limited, flow-cycled: every breath is started by the patient and the machine adds a set pressure above PEEP.
Breath ends when inspiratory flow falls to a set % of peak (cycle-off, often 25%); raise it in COPD to shorten inspiration.
Tidal volume depends on support level, compliance, resistance and patient effort, so it varies breath to breath.
No guaranteed minute ventilation: set apnoea back-up; watch for over-assist (low RR, big VT) and under-assist (fast shallow breathing).
items.pearl: Used for weaning and SBT (e.g. PS 5–8 cmH2O + PEEP 5).
